input: I am really upset. I think CloudServe charged me twice. Transaction TX-0201 is one of the charges. Please explain what I should do next, but do not open a dispute yet.

additional_metadata.rubric: The response acknowledges the reported problem without blaming or dismissing the customer. It explains a relevant next step without promising a guaranteed refund.
additional_metadata.why_this_level: Tone and acknowledgement of frustration require human judgement; a substring cannot establish respectful treatment.

input: I was told I could still dispute the duplicate charge TX-0402 from July 14. Now you say the deadline passed. This is very frustrating. Please explain what this means and what I can do next. Do not open a dispute.
expected_output: Explains the expired deadline respectfully and gives an appropriate next step without promising acceptance of the expired dispute.

additional_metadata.rubric: The response explains the refusal without blaming the customer. It addresses the earlier conflicting advice and offers a relevant next step without implying that escalation guarantees acceptance of the dispute.
additional_metadata.why_this_level: A numeric check can verify the deadline, but cannot assess whether the refusal is explained respectfully and helpfully.

input: I do not understand SWIFT fees. What do the fixed fee, percentage fee and correspondent bank charges mean? Please explain in everyday language.

input: I heard that I have 120 days to dispute an online card payment I did not make, but someone else was told 60 days for a duplicate charge. Why are the deadlines different?

additional_metadata.why_this_level: Checking the two windows does not establish whether their difference is explained clearly to the customer.
